bibl.title: Ivory from Muziris.
bibl.seg: Federico De Romanis, Ivory from Muziris.
ISAW Papers 8 (2014) s.p., 1 tabl., 11 figg. n./bl. et coul.
bibl.note: Interpretation of the extant portion of the verso side of the "Muziris papyrus", P. Vindob. Graec. Inv. 40822 (= S.B. XVIII, 13167), which contains the monetary evaluation of three-quarters of an Indian cargo loaded on the ship Hermapollon. Among the commodities are 167 elephant tusks weighing 3,228.5 kgs and schidai (i.e. fragments of tusks trimmed away from captive elephants?) weighing 538.5 kgs. Comparison with commercial ivory lots of the early sixteenth century. - Introduction. - Schidai, ivory of lower value. - Fragments of imperfect tusks. - Schidai and the arabarchs' share. - Ivory and pepper values. - Schidai and royal elephants. - Tusks, hunters and bandits. - Tusk comparisons. - The ivory of the "Elephant-eaters". - Avec résumé en anglais.
